7:54.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ يُغۡشِي ٱلَّيۡلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ يَطۡلُبُهُۥ حَثِيثࣰ ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ وَٱلنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَٰتِۭ بِأَمۡرِهِۦٓۗ أَلَا لَهُ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ وَٱلۡأَمۡرُۗ تَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
7:54.en: Lo! your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, then mounted He the Throne. He covereth the night with the day, which is in haste to follow it, and hath made the sun and the moon and the stars subservient by His command. His verily is all creation and commandment. Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

2:214.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأۡتِكُم مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۖ مَّسَّتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءُ وَٱلضَّرَّآءُ وَزُلۡزِلُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ مَتَىٰ نَصۡرُ ٱللَّهِۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ نَصۡرَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبࣱ‏
2:214.en: Or think ye that ye will enter paradise while yet there hath not come unto you the like of (that which came to) those who passed away before you? Affliction and adversity befell them, they were shaken as with earthquake, till the messenger (of Allah) and those who believed along with him said: When cometh Allah's help? Now surely Allah's help is nigh

ifCZTJvTc0k.title: Important Messages for the Committed
ifCZTJvTc0k.one_line: Forty-five days into the Gaza war, he gives those newly committed to the cause three points: identity endures, we will outlast you, and don't hasten Allah.
ifCZTJvTc0k.summary: He speaks only to those who, since the war on Gaza began some 45 days earlier, have resolved to commit their lives to their faith and its causes; anyone still unmoved, he says, will not be moved by another speech. Lasting change takes time, as creation in six days teaches, so patience means committed work through a long process, not waiting. Any single act of oppression should be enough to commit a Muslim to justice for life. His first point is that attempts to erase Muslim identity, values and principles are centuries old and keep failing, because Muslims keep filling masajid, raising families and educating children despite every flaw. The world wants a toothless Muslim content with a corrupt status quo. Second, the message to the world is that we will outlast you, through the grit the Prophet modelled. When Abu Talib begged him to ease off, the Prophet answered that he could no more stop than someone could light a flame from the sun. The Prophet never scheduled time off, retirement is a strange idea, and 'I'm busy' only means something is not a priority; Islam is not a part-time gym membership. Finally, do not hasten Allah; hasten yourself and ask what you are failing to do.

outline.heading: Opening
A bond the world does not see
outline.gist: He speaks to those who have made decisions about their commitment since the war began; with 15,000 killed, the world does not grasp how deeply Muslims mourn one another and any life taken unjustly.

outline.heading: Change takes time: creation in six days
outline.gist: Complex problems need long-term commitment; Allah created in six days because we, not He, live in time, so patience means persisting in the work, not sitting and waiting.

outline.heading: If this did not wake you, nothing will
outline.gist: He will not keep selling commitment to the unmoved; 45 days hold enough realizations for a lifetime, so what more is needed, the masjid in rubble or the Kaaba in ruins?

outline.heading: Any act of oppression is enough
outline.gist: For a Muslim not even one innocent life is needed; any oppression commits him to justice for life, let alone Gaza, Syria, Iraq and Afghanistan.

outline.heading: Point one: centuries of attempts on Muslim identity
outline.gist: Attempts to erase Muslim language, culture, values and principles, some backed by the world's major powers, are innumerable and centuries old, yet Islam survives.

outline.heading: They want a toothless Muslim
outline.gist: Muslims are targeted because they stand for justice against a corrupt status quo that suits the wealthy; the real erasure is of that edge, leaving Muslims who just pray and leave.

outline.heading: Why the attempts keep failing
outline.gist: A Muslim who resists is a different story; the attempts fail because Muslims keep coming to their masajid, raising families and educating their youth, with all the flaws that come with it.

outline.heading: When Muslims give up on justice
outline.gist: This will only stop when Muslims abandon justice and righteousness; then the countdown to the end of times begins, a time with no justice when oppression breeds hatred and people stop thinking rationally.

outline.heading: Our causes do not die
outline.gist: The attempts will keep testing whether we compromise, but however many are killed we keep building families and filling masajid; even when weak, our causes stay alive in the hearts that carry them.

outline.heading: Point two: we will outlast you
outline.gist: The Prophet had no advantage in numbers, wealth or connections, only grit and relentlessness, and he outlasted them; you are defeated only when you quit, so keep speaking the truth whatever it costs.

outline.heading: Palestine is the tip of the iceberg
outline.gist: It is the injustice in plain sight; the deeper you dig the more you find, so a Muslim has his work cut out.

outline.heading: Abu Talib and the flame from the sun
outline.gist: Under Quraysh's pressure even Abu Talib asked him to ease off; with a tear the Prophet said he could no more stop than they could light a flame from the sun, a lesson that only Allah truly stands by you.

outline.heading: Retirement is when you are dead
outline.gist: The Prophet never scheduled vacations or lived for the next break; say you no longer need to earn and can now focus on what you are here for.

outline.heading: Your time belongs to Allah
outline.gist: Taking causes beyond local platforms needs creativity and cannot happen in a half-committed society; even work is done because He commanded it.

outline.heading: "I'm busy" means not a priority
outline.gist: When someone says they had no time, they mean it did not make their list; what you prioritize you do every time.

outline.heading: Islam is not a part-time gym membership
outline.gist: Admitting your priorities honestly brings hope of change; the world wants a quiet Muslim content with the status quo, but that is not why the Prophet built masajid or taught the Quran.

outline.heading: Interlude
Final point: hasten yourself, not Allah
outline.gist: Asking why Allah has not acted yet is a waste of time and borderline rude; ask instead why you have not acted and what you are waiting for.

outline.heading: Even those beside the prophets asked "when?"
outline.gist: People doing everything right alongside their prophets asked when Allah's help would come and were told it is near; my part is to hurry myself.

outline.heading: Outro

60:4.ar: قَدۡ كَانَتۡ لَكُمۡ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةࣱ فِيٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِذۡ قَالُواْ لِقَوۡمِهِمۡ إِنَّا بُرَءَٰٓؤُاْ مِنكُمۡ وَمِمَّا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَفَرۡنَا بِكُمۡ وَبَدَا بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَكُمُ ٱلۡعَدَٰوَةُ وَٱلۡبَغۡضَآءُ أَبَدًا حَتَّىٰ تُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَحۡدَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَوۡلَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ لَأَسۡتَغۡفِرَنَّ لَكَ وَمَآ أَمۡلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۖ رَّبَّنَا عَلَيۡكَ تَوَكَّلۡنَا وَإِلَيۡكَ أَنَبۡنَا وَإِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
60:4.en: There is a goodly pattern for you in Abraham and those with him, when they told their folk: Lo! we are guiltless of you and all that ye worship beside Allah. We have done with you. And there hath arisen between us and you hostility and hate for ever until ye believe in Allah only - save that which Abraham promised his father (when he said): I will ask forgiveness for thee, though I own nothing for thee from Allah - Our Lord! In Thee we put our trust, and unto Thee we turn repentant, and unto Thee is the journeying

60:5.ar: رَبَّنَا لَا تَجۡعَلۡنَا فِتۡنَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا رَبَّنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
60:5.en: Our Lord! Make us not a prey for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord! Lo! Thou, only Thou, are the Mighty, the Wise

60:6.ar: لَقَدۡ كَانَ لَكُمۡ فِيهِمۡ أُسۡوَةٌ حَسَنَةࣱ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلۡيَوۡمَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ ٱلۡحَمِيدُ
60:6.en: Verily ye have in them a goodly pattern for everyone who looketh to Allah and the Last Day. And whosoever may turn away, lo! still Allah, He is the Absolute, the Owner of Praise

60:7.ar: ۞عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَجۡعَلَ بَيۡنَكُمۡ وَبَيۡنَ ٱلَّذِينَ عَادَيۡتُم مِّنۡهُم مَّوَدَّةࣰۚ وَٱللَّهُ قَدِيرࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
60:7.en: It may be that Allah will ordain love between you and those of them with whom ye are at enmity. Allah is Mighty, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

4:77.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمۡ كُفُّوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَكُمۡ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ إِذَا فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَخۡشَوۡنَ ٱلنَّاسَ كَخَشۡيَةِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡ أَشَدَّ خَشۡيَةࣰۚ وَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَا لِمَ كَتَبۡتَ عَلَيۡنَا ٱلۡقِتَالَ لَوۡلَآ أَخَّرۡتَنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ قَرِيبࣲۗ قُلۡ مَتَٰعُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا قَلِيلࣱ وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ خَيۡرࣱ لِّمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰ وَلَا تُظۡلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا
4:77.en: Hast thou not seen those unto whom it was said: Withhold your hands, establish worship and pay the poordue, but when fighting was prescribed for them behold! a party of them fear mankind even as their fear of Allah or with greater fear, and say: Our Lord! Why hast Thou ordained fighting for us? If only Thou wouldst give us respite yet a while! Say (unto them, O Muhammad): The comfort of this world is scant; the Hereafter will be better for him who wardeth off (evil); and ye will not be wronged the down upon a date-stone

c28qq1WO9Y4.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Mumtahinah, Part 2: Verses 4-7
c28qq1WO9Y4.one_line: Ibrahim as the model for drawing a line with oppressors, the Holy Land as a shared home, and Allah's promise to one day place love between enemies.
c28qq1WO9Y4.summary: He continues Al-Mumtahinah's argument that Muslims must know where to draw the line with those who deny their fundamental rights, while their baseline toward others remains compassion. Uswah means deep emulation, understanding how a role model thought rather than copying outward actions. Ibrahim's people tried to burn and then expelled him, which leads into a long aside: the Holy Land has always been open to both sons of Ibrahim, Middle Eastern Muslims lived with Jewish neighbours for centuries, Jews left Andalusia with the Muslims, and Palestine is a question of oppression, not religion. Ibrahim's disavowal rejects the oppressor's narrative and places the burden of change on the oppressor; he compares this to abuse, where the victim must stop blaming themselves. The one exception, Ibrahim's prayer for his father, reassures the over-compassionate companions. Their prayer not to be made a trial for the disbelievers shows they did not even want their enemies to become persecutors. Verse 6 stresses that this is for the believers' own benefit, since Allah needs nothing. Verse 7, among his favourite verses, promises that Allah may place love between them and their enemies, a promise that only becomes possible once the line is drawn now. He urges listeners to dream of that day while demanding change from oppressors, not from the oppressed.

outline.heading: Review: three categories of non-Muslims and the compassionate baseline
outline.gist: Muslims celebrate conversions and hold no animosity toward other faiths, but the Quran ensures they do not cave on fundamental rights.

outline.heading: Finding the balance and drawing the line
outline.gist: People swing between naive openness and aggression; failing to draw a line invites abuse, individually as well as communally.

outline.heading: Review of verses 1-3
outline.gist: Those who deny your rights will crush you once they have the upper hand, and kinship will not help.

outline.heading: Interlude
Uswah: emulation that understands how they thought
outline.gist: Uswah comes from feeling for someone; following the Prophet means grasping his context and outlook, otherwise the same act yields a different outcome.

outline.heading: Addressed to the Prophet's community after Hatib's letter
outline.gist: 'Those with him' may mean Ibrahim's believers or everyone in his story; the example answers the companions' difficulty drawing a line.

outline.heading: Freedom of belief is freedom of expression
outline.gist: Inner belief cannot be controlled, so the real right is to express it, one of the five things Islam preserves; denying it is a deal breaker.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's people did what Quraysh did
outline.gist: They tried to burn him for his argument and expelled him, denying him belief, life and home.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's journey and the land promised to his children
outline.gist: He travelled from Iraq through Sham, Egypt and Mecca; the land was always shared by the children of Isma'il and Ishaq.

outline.heading: The Holy Land as a diverse, welcoming home
outline.gist: Jewish communities lived well in Middle Eastern capitals for centuries; the problem is one group expelling the other and denying their lineage.

outline.heading: Palestine is a question of oppression, not religion
outline.gist: Muslims have no hostility to Judaism; framing it as a religious conflict was a mistake that serves the opposing narrative.

outline.heading: Andalusia: the Jews left with the Muslims
outline.gist: After the expulsion from Iberia, Jewish communities followed Muslims to North Africa, while Muslims who stayed were brutally persecuted.

outline.heading: A clearer narrative is emerging
outline.gist: Muslims are educating themselves and voicing the Palestinian narrative, which may shift the world within decades.

outline.heading: Disavowal: rejecting the oppressor's narrative
outline.gist: Ibrahim, the first Muslim, uses kufr for rejecting their theology; it is a refusal of an oppressive narrative, not a curse.

outline.heading: 'Until you believe': the change must come from the oppressor
outline.gist: Muslims normally ask what they could do better, but under persecution the line is drawn and the burden shifts to the oppressor.

outline.heading: The same line in abusive relationships
outline.gist: Abuse victims keep blaming themselves; ordinary marital disputes differ from abuse, and people should seek guidance before deciding.

outline.heading: The exception: Ibrahim's prayer for his father
outline.gist: Allah notes even Ibrahim had a soft spot, reassuring the companions that their excess of compassion was not far off.

outline.heading: Enmity is about denial of rights, not mere disbelief
outline.gist: His father became an enemy through persecution; verses 8-9 make the distinction explicit.

outline.heading: 'Do not make us a trial for the disbelievers'
outline.gist: Relying on and returning to Allah, they ask not to be persecuted, partly so their enemies do not become persecutors bound for punishment.

outline.heading: Interlude
A good example for those who hope for Allah and the Last Day
outline.gist: The added emphasis addresses later believers: learn from the Prophet and Ibrahim, including from their mistakes.

outline.heading: Whoever turns away: Allah needs no one
outline.gist: Drawing the line means confrontation, which is hard; Allah reminds them it is for their own preservation.

outline.heading: Al-Ghani al-Hamid
outline.gist: Allah is independent and praiseworthy whether people obey or not, so His commands serve their interest.

outline.heading: Those who asked to be spared from fighting
outline.gist: Told to hold back in Mecca and to defend themselves in Medina, some asked for delay; the world is short, so stand for what matters.

outline.heading: Perhaps Allah will place love between you and your enemies
outline.gist: The surah circles back to love: after telling them to withhold it, Allah sets love with the enemy as the goal.

outline.heading: Allah is capable and forgiving: love only after the line
outline.gist: Love becomes possible only if the line is drawn now; Allah eases a hard command for a loving community.

outline.heading: Mawaddah, not merely peace
outline.gist: Allah chose the word for love itself; he challenges anyone to find scripture or charter that matches this.

outline.heading: The danger of following a book you have not read
outline.gist: Critics and Muslims alike misrepresent Islam because they have not read these verses.

outline.heading: 'Asa from Allah means it will happen
outline.gist: Words of probability become certainty when attributed to Allah; it may take long, through conflict, but love will return.

outline.heading: Forgiveness that softens hearts
outline.gist: Allah fills hearts with tenderness so people can forgive; dream of that day, but demand change from the oppressor, never the oppressed.

60:10.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا جَآءَكُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتُ مُهَٰجِرَٰتࣲ فَٱمۡتَحِنُوهُنَّۖ ٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِإِيمَٰنِهِنَّۖ فَإِنۡ عَلِمۡتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤۡمِنَٰتࣲ فَلَا تَرۡجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى ٱلۡكُفَّارِۖ لَا هُنَّ حِلࣱّ لَّهُمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحِلُّونَ لَهُنَّۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مَّآ أَنفَقُواْۚ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَن تَنكِحُوهُنَّ إِذَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّۚ وَلَا تُمۡسِكُواْ بِعِصَمِ ٱلۡكَوَافِرِ وَسۡـَٔلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقۡتُمۡ وَلۡيَسۡـَٔلُواْ مَآ أَنفَقُواْۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ حُكۡمُ ٱللَّهِ يَحۡكُمُ بَيۡنَكُمۡۖ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
60:10.en: O ye who believe! When believing women come unto you as fugitives, examine them. Allah is Best Aware of their faith. Then, if ye know them for true believers, send them not back unto the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them (the disbelievers), nor are they (the disbelievers) lawful for them. And give them (the disbelievers) that which they have spent (upon them). And it is no sin for you to marry such women when ye have given them their dues. And hold not to the ties of disbelieving women; and ask for (the return of) that which ye have spent; and let them (the disbelievers) ask for that which they have spent. That is the judgment of Allah. He judgeth between you. Allah is Knower, Wise

60:11.ar: وَإِن فَاتَكُمۡ شَيۡءࣱ مِّنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡكُفَّارِ فَعَاقَبۡتُمۡ فَـَٔاتُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ذَهَبَتۡ أَزۡوَٰجُهُم مِّثۡلَ مَآ أَنفَقُواْۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنتُم بِهِۦ مُؤۡمِنُونَ
60:11.en: And if any of your wives have gone from you unto the disbelievers and afterward ye have your turn (of triumph), then give unto those whose wives have gone the like of that which they have spent, and keep your duty to Allah in Whom ye are believers

60:12.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتُ يُبَايِعۡنَكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن لَّا يُشۡرِكۡنَ بِٱللَّهِ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَسۡرِقۡنَ وَلَا يَزۡنِينَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلۡنَ أَوۡلَٰدَهُنَّ وَلَا يَأۡتِينَ بِبُهۡتَٰنࣲ يَفۡتَرِينَهُۥ بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِنَّ وَأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ وَلَا يَعۡصِينَكَ فِي مَعۡرُوفࣲ فَبَايِعۡهُنَّ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُنَّ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
60:12.en: O Prophet! If believing women come unto thee, taking oath of allegiance unto thee that they will ascribe no thing as partner unto Allah, and will neither steal nor commit adultery nor kill their children, nor produce any lie that they have devised between their hands and feet, nor disobey thee in what is right, then accept their allegiance and ask Allah to forgive them. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

60:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ قَوۡمًا غَضِبَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ قَدۡ يَئِسُواْ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ كَمَا يَئِسَ ٱلۡكُفَّارُ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡقُبُورِ
60:13.en: O ye who believe! Be not friendly with a folk with whom Allah is wroth, (a folk) who have despaired of the Hereafter as the disbelievers despair of those who are in the graves

60:8.ar: لَّا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمۡ يُخۡرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمۡ وَتُقۡسِطُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
60:8.en: Allah forbiddeth you not those who warred not against you on account of religion and drove you not out from your homes, that ye should show them kindness and deal justly with them. Lo! Allah loveth the just dealers

60:9.ar: إِنَّمَا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ قَٰتَلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَأَخۡرَجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ وَظَٰهَرُواْ عَلَىٰٓ إِخۡرَاجِكُمۡ أَن تَوَلَّوۡهُمۡۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهُمۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
60:9.en: Allah forbiddeth you only those who warred against you on account of religion and have driven you out from your homes and helped to drive you out, that ye make friends of them. Whosoever maketh friends of them - (All) such are wrong-doers

60:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ تُلۡقُونَ إِلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡمَوَدَّةِ وَقَدۡ كَفَرُواْ بِمَا جَآءَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ يُخۡرِجُونَ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَإِيَّاكُمۡ أَن تُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ رَبِّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ خَرَجۡتُمۡ جِهَٰدࣰ ا فِي سَبِيلِي وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ مَرۡضَاتِيۚ تُسِرُّونَ إِلَيۡهِم بِٱلۡمَوَدَّةِ وَأَنَا۠ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَآ أَخۡفَيۡتُمۡ وَمَآ أَعۡلَنتُمۡۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡهُ مِنكُمۡ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ سَوَآءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ
60:1.en: O ye who believe! Choose not My enemy and your enemy for allies. Do ye give them friendship when they disbelieve in that truth which hath come unto you, driving out the messenger and you because ye believe in Allah, your Lord? If ye have come forth to strive in My way and seeking My good pleasure, (show them not friendship). Do ye show friendship unto them in secret, when I am Best Aware of what ye hide and what ye proclaim? And whosoever doeth it among you, he verily hath strayed from the right way

60:5.ar: رَبَّنَا لَا تَجۡعَلۡنَا فِتۡنَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا رَبَّنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
60:5.en: Our Lord! Make us not a prey for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord! Lo! Thou, only Thou, are the Mighty, the Wise

R0mzGjurslA.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Mumtahinah, Part 4: Verses 10-13
R0mzGjurslA.one_line: Concluding Al-Mumtahinah: why the Quran forbids rather than commands, fairness even to hostile husbands, women's independent place in the ummah, and the women's pledge.
R0mzGjurslA.summary: He recaps the surah's three categories of non-Muslims and explains why it phrases the rules as it does: a prohibition removes one option and leaves all others open, while 'Allah does not forbid you' sets a minimum and invites more. Muslims' conduct depends on how others treat them, not on Muslim strength, and a command only makes sense if Muslims were doing the opposite, which shows they kept extending friendship to their persecutors. He calls the bloodthirsty image of Islam a colonial device and repeats that normalisation with persecutors violates a clear, unabrogated rule. On verses 10-11 he dwells on paying back hostile husbands' dowries out of Muslim funds, giving the emigrant women their own mahr, and the ruling on wives who stayed behind. He argues these details established something new in Arabia: a woman could join the ummah on her own, single and independent, as Umm Kulthum, daughter of one of the Prophet's fiercest enemies, did. He also discusses who holds the right to end a marriage. The women's pledge in verse 12 is ethical rather than ritual, and he stresses that worship without honesty achieves nothing. He defends motherhood against being dismissed and tells of Hind bint Utbah's pledge, then closes on verse 13, which returns to the opening command against alliance.

outline.heading: Opening
Review: combative and non-combative non-Muslims
outline.gist: Fiqh distinguishes harbi enemies from non-combatants; without that distinction verses get misused.

outline.heading: Why the Quran prefers prohibitions
outline.gist: Forbidding one act leaves every other option open, giving flexibility across times and places.

outline.heading: Conquest of Mecca: forgiveness once in power
outline.gist: With the upper hand the Prophet pardoned almost everyone; only a handful were excluded and most of them were later forgiven.

outline.heading: 'Not forbidden' sets the minimum
outline.gist: The double negative makes birr and justice the least owed to non-combatants, while the prohibition on alliance also covers anything beyond it.

outline.heading: Relations depend on their conduct, not our strength
outline.gist: No conditions are placed on Muslims' wealth or power; only a change in how others treat them changes the rule, as with Ibrahim.

outline.heading: A surah that opens and closes on alliance
outline.gist: The command not to take enemies as allies frames the surah and reveals that Muslims tended to do so.

outline.heading: Commands fit their context: the sibling analogy
outline.gist: You only tell a mistreated child to stop being kind to an aggressive sibling, so the command shows Muslims were too kind.

outline.heading: Muslims kept extending their hand
outline.gist: The Quran taught them to wish guidance even for enemies mid-battle, then restricted that where they had to stand firm.

outline.heading: The bloodthirsty image is a colonial device
outline.gist: Making peoples ashamed of their identity is an old colonial tactic; debunking it restores Muslims' confidence and dawah.

outline.heading: Not wanting to be anyone's trial
outline.gist: Standing firm prevents weakness that leads to persecution, which harms both sides.

outline.heading: Normalisation violates a clear, unabrogated rule
outline.gist: After tens of thousands killed, building alliances with those who deny Palestinians their humanity is indefensible; no scholar treated these verses as abrogated.

outline.heading: The closing verses: emigrant women after Hudaybiyyah
outline.gist: They show a striking fairness toward combative non-Muslims.

outline.heading: Screening for spies: do your best
outline.gist: Some women had come only to gather intelligence; the Quran teaches doing one's best even when it cannot be certain.

outline.heading: Paying hostile husbands from Muslim funds
outline.gist: The dowries were repaid from the community's own wealth, a wartime fairness he says has no equal.

outline.heading: Accept a little oppression and the door never closes
outline.gist: Amounts do not matter once injustice is tolerated, as with children fighting where both are at fault.

outline.heading: Enmity is no licence for injustice
outline.gist: Forbidding alliance never permits mistreating the enemy.

outline.heading: Marrying the emigrant women with their own mahr
outline.gist: Paying her husband does not put her in debt; whoever marries her must give her own dowry.

outline.heading: Who holds the right to end a marriage
outline.gist: Marriage needs both parties' agreement but one holds 'isma; it can be agreed to rest with the wife, and many men misuse it.

outline.heading: Why divorce usually rests with the husband
outline.gist: It lies with whoever is less likely to end the union in anger; a mother's emotional depth is what raises children.

outline.heading: Wives who stayed behind
outline.gist: Muslim men end marriages to combative wives who refused to join them and may ask for their dowries back.

outline.heading: Women join the ummah in their own right
outline.gist: A Muslim woman was no longer an accessory to a man; living single outside one's tribe was unheard of in Arabia.

outline.heading: Umm Kulthum, daughter of the Prophet's fiercest enemy
outline.gist: Her father had persecuted the Prophet most harshly; the Prophet paid her dowry back and she lived independently in Medina.

outline.heading: Breaking a ceiling in Arabian society
outline.gist: A woman seeking refuge was normally returned, enslaved or married off; now she could stay free and unmarried.

outline.heading: Interlude
When Quraysh refused to repay Muslim husbands
outline.gist: If wealth is later recovered, Muslim men whose wives stayed behind are compensated first.

outline.heading: Fairness to everyone to secure the new norm
outline.gist: The detailed rules protected each party so the change for women could stand whoever disliked it.

outline.heading: Interlude
The pledge is taken by the leader
outline.gist: Addressed to the Prophet as leader, bay'ah is spiritual before it is political and belongs to leadership.

outline.heading: First term: associate nothing with Allah
outline.gist: Tawhid stands alone in importance; with it a person can hope despite much else lacking.

outline.heading: The pledge at Aqabah
outline.gist: The Prophet took almost the same pledge from twelve men of Medina, insisting the Aws be included so he came as leader of all.

outline.heading: An ethical pledge, not a ritual one
outline.gist: No theft, zina, killing children or false attribution of paternity; prayer and tears mean little while one cheats and lies.

outline.heading: Women as the foundation of social stability
outline.gist: Loyalty, chastity and clear lineage hold families together, and society unravels without them.

outline.heading: 'Just a mother'?
outline.gist: Nurturing life is the greatest work; his own work means nothing if his wife's work at home fails.

outline.heading: Obedience in what is right, and how the pledge was given
outline.gist: Women pledge not to disobey him in good; he took the pledge by word without shaking hands and prayed for their forgiveness.

outline.heading: Conquest of Mecca: Hind bint Utbah's pledge
outline.gist: Veiled, she answered each term with sharp remarks about idols, Abu Sufyan's money, zina and her sons killed at Badr, then committed never to disobey.

outline.heading: Ending as it began: no alliance with persecutors
outline.gist: Those under Allah's wrath for persecution have no hope in the Hereafter; the surah defines relations with combatants, non-combatants and converts.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Muslims repaid hostile husbands' dowries; tolerating any oppression opens a door that never closes.

themes.label: Gender relations, chastity and modesty

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Women's role in stable families is the base of society, and motherhood is not lesser work.

60:7.en: It may be that Allah will ordain love between you and those of them with whom ye are at enmity. Allah is Mighty, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

60:10.en: O ye who believe! When believing women come unto you as fugitives, examine them. Allah is Best Aware of their faith. Then, if ye know them for true believers, send them not back unto the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them (the disbelievers), nor are they (the disbelievers) lawful for them. And give them (the disbelievers) that which they have spent (upon them). And it is no sin for you to marry such women when ye have given them their dues. And hold not to the ties of disbelieving women; and ask for (the return of) that which ye have spent; and let them (the disbelievers) ask for that which they have spent. That is the judgment of Allah. He judgeth between you. Allah is Knower, Wise

2:143.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَسَطࣰ ا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ اۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:143.en: Thus We have appointed you a middle nation, that ye may be witnesses against mankind, and that the messenger may be a witness against you. And We appointed the qiblah which ye formerly observed only that We might know him who followeth the messenger, from him who turneth on his heels. In truth it was a hard (test) save for those whom Allah guided. But it was not Allah's purpose that your faith should be in vain, for Allah is Full of Pity, Merciful toward mankind

toKKBIGlVsc.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Mumtahinah, Part 3: Verses 8-10
toKKBIGlVsc.one_line: Al-Mumtahinah 8-9 as the governing rule with non-Muslims: kindness and justice for all, with alliance forbidden only with persecutors; normalisation; and the women emigrants.
toKKBIGlVsc.summary: After reviewing the surah's opening argument and the five necessities every Islamic ruling protects, he reads verse 7 as almost a dua and notes that Allah's forgiveness can include softening the heart of the one who was wronged. Verses 8-9 then state the rule plainly. Allah does not forbid birr, the highest kindness, and qist, justice with generosity, toward anyone who has not fought Muslims over their faith or driven them from their homes. With 'innama' He exclusively forbids one thing, alliance, with three groups: those who deny Muslims' faith, those who expel them, and those who back them. Belief itself is never the criterion. Allying with persecutors is weakness, not compassion, and this is the balanced middle way. He applies it to normalisation with the occupation of Palestine, citing the toll in Gaza and child prisoners, insists that no person has authority over the Quran to set such verses aside, and notes that even modest advocacy has changed the conversation. Verse 10 addresses believing women who emigrated after Hudaybiyyah: test their sincerity, do not return them, and still repay their hostile husbands' dowries, showing that forbidden alliance never permits injustice. He tells the stories of Umm Kulthum and Abu Basir along the way.

outline.heading: Review: the cluster and the first seven verses
outline.gist: Al-Mumtahinah organises relations with combative and non-combative non-Muslims and converts; the opening argued against loving those who deny Muslims' rights.

outline.heading: The five necessities every ruling protects
outline.gist: Life, intellect, wealth, honour and freedom of belief and expression; without them there is no safety or order.

outline.heading: Verse 7 as a dua, and forgiveness that reaches the wronged
outline.gist: 'Asa can be read as a prayer; when Allah forgives a wrong against others He also fills the victim's heart with forgiveness.

outline.heading: Short Medinan surahs as summaries of the Quran's principles
outline.gist: These surahs condense what longer surahs explain at length, so knowing them gives the core values.

outline.heading: Interlude
Tajweed: giving each letter its due
outline.gist: A light sin next to a heavy ta must stay light; most of tajweed is keeping letters pure from their neighbours, as the Prophet recited letter by letter.

outline.heading: From general attitude to explicit rule
outline.gist: The opening showed the attitude; verses 8-9 state exactly where the line is drawn.

outline.heading: Those who did not fight you over faith or expel you
outline.gist: Freedom of religion only means something as freedom to express it; those who respect it and your home fall under the permission.

outline.heading: Birr and qist: the best conduct and generous justice
outline.gist: Birr, the word used for parents, is permitted toward non-Muslims; qist is justice delivered with kindness, and Allah loves it.

outline.heading: 'Innama': alliance is the only thing forbidden
outline.gist: Allah exclusively forbids alliance with those who fought you over faith, expelled you, or backed your expulsion.

outline.heading: Belief is not the criterion
outline.gist: Neither verse mentions belief or disbelief; relations depend on conduct toward Muslims' rights.

outline.heading: Allying with persecutors is weakness, not compassion
outline.gist: The surah worries not that Muslims will lose compassion but that they will fail to recognise persecutors.

outline.heading: A rule for any nation that wants to survive
outline.gist: Muslims repeated the mistake centuries later; any entity that will not defend its basic rights eventually ceases to exist.

outline.heading: The middle way between naivety and hostility
outline.gist: People swing between loving those who deny their humanity and losing compassion even for fellow Muslims; the verses set the balance.

outline.heading: Treat others normally; the hard third group
outline.gist: With non-persecutors ordinary relations apply; cutting ties with those who support persecution is harder but still required.

outline.heading: One ummah: persecuting some is persecuting all
outline.gist: Recent weeks will make this the headline issue; inner hope for their guidance and dawah remain fine, alliances do not.

outline.heading: Normalisation is the forbidden alliance
outline.gist: Financial, military and social alliances normalise occupation and racism; the Quran's wording leaves no room for argument.

outline.heading: Standing your ground and the shifting conversation
outline.gist: Love can return once persecution ends; even modest advocacy has changed the conversation about Palestine.

outline.heading: A generation that grew up with normalisation
outline.gist: Once no Muslim leader would publicly normalise; now nations, groups and even scholars do.

outline.heading: The Quran has authority over us, not the reverse
outline.gist: No person may decide which verses apply; giving a human that power is how practices without basis appear.

outline.heading: Only one thing, and it is exactly what is done
outline.gist: Social contact and dialogue are allowed; political and financial alliance with persecutors erodes dignity.

outline.heading: Extend your hand only as an equal
outline.gist: Alliance is possible with enemies who do not deny each other's rights; this question will be central in the coming decade.

outline.heading: Gaza's dead children and child prisoners
outline.gist: Thousands of civilians and children killed and minors held for years without family or fair process define persecution.

outline.heading: A hand offered from under the boot is surrender
outline.gist: Weakness may prevent fighting back, but refusing alliance preserves integrity; the verses' precision shows divine wisdom.

outline.heading: Interlude
Treaty of Hudaybiyyah: the clause on those who flee to Medina
outline.gist: Those leaving Mecca without permission were to be returned; the treaty did not specify women, and this verse does.

outline.heading: Test the women emigrants
outline.gist: Some had come claiming Islam to gather intelligence, so they were screened; only Allah knows hearts.

outline.heading: Umm Kulthum's emigration
outline.gist: Her husband and brother demanded her return; the Prophet showed the treaty did not cover women and refused.

outline.heading: Abu Basir's coastal band and Abu Jandal
outline.gist: Men sent back formed a group on the Red Sea coast raiding Quraysh's caravans until Quraysh asked to drop the clause; women had no such option.

outline.heading: No longer lawful for one another
outline.gist: Believing women are not returned and the marriages to pagan husbands end.

outline.heading: Repay the hostile husbands' dowries
outline.gist: Since the wife ends the marriage, the dowry is returned, as in a wife-initiated divorce.

outline.heading: No alliance, but never injustice
outline.gist: Even toward persecutors Muslims must be fair; forbidden alliance is not licence to oppress.

5:21.ar: يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ ٱلۡمُقَدَّسَةَ ٱلَّتِي كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ وَلَا تَرۡتَدُّواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَدۡبَارِكُمۡ فَتَنقَلِبُواْ خَٰسِرِينَ
5:21.en: O my people! Go into the holy land which Allah hath ordained for you. Turn not in flight, for surely ye turn back as losers

5:22.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوۡمࣰ ا جَبَّارِينَ وَإِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَا حَتَّىٰ يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِن يَخۡرُجُواْ مِنۡهَا فَإِنَّا دَٰخِلُونَ
5:22.en: They said: O Moses! Lo! a giant people (dwell) therein and lo! we go not in till they go forth from thence. When they go forth from thence, then we will enter (not till then)

5:23.ar: قَالَ رَجُلَانِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِمَا ٱدۡخُلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡبَابَ فَإِذَا دَخَلۡتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمۡ غَٰلِبُونَۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوٓاْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
5:23.en: Then out spake two of those who feared (their Lord, men) unto whom Allah had been gracious: Enter in upon them by the gate, for if ye enter by it, lo! ye will be victorious. So put your trust (in Allah) if ye are indeed believers

5:24.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَن نَّدۡخُلَهَآ أَبَدࣰ ا مَّا دَامُواْ فِيهَا فَٱذۡهَبۡ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَٰتِلَآ إِنَّا هَٰهُنَا قَٰعِدُونَ
5:24.en: They said: O Moses! We will never enter (the land) while they are in it. So go thou and thy Lord and fight! We will sit here

5:26.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡۛ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰۛ يَتِيهُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ فَلَا تَأۡسَ عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:26.en: (Their Lord) said: For this the land will surely be forbidden them for forty years that they will wander in the earth, bewildered. So grieve not over the wrongdoing folk

l0R7cxwnU1I.title: The Laws of Success/Victory 1: Getting Our House in Order
l0R7cxwnU1I.one_line: As bombing of Gaza resumes, he argues change starts by getting our local house in order, and introduces his Al-Anfal series on the laws of victory.
l0R7cxwnU1I.summary: With the bombing of Gaza resuming after a short ceasefire, he calls it a test of longevity: Muslims care during the acute phase and then return to baseline. Worldwide protests show the will of a people being ignored because it lacks proper channels. We cannot control world leaders or scholars, but we can control our own conduct and community. If you cannot clean up your own backyard, a city of about 35,000 Muslims, spare everyone your theories for fixing the world. Islam spread because the Prophet proved in Madinah that his model worked: a diverse society of rights, ethics, sacrifice and selflessness that visitors came to see. Because his house was in order, Islam went from a spot to a splash across three continents in a few decades. Claiming to stand for Palestine while doing nothing locally is not honest, and people will ask why this beautiful message is not working for us. Unlike the Israelites sent to wander forty years, this generation only needs to decide what its life is about and make Islam the main project. In the second khutbah he says Islam is a cause, not only rituals, and that people committed to justice are hard to control or distract. He then introduces the Al-Anfal series: strength must come from within individuals and communities.

outline.heading: Opening
The bombing resumes: a test of longevity
outline.gist: After a short ceasefire and 15,000 killed, random bombing of civilians returns. Advocacy only has value when it is prepared for the long haul, and Allah is testing whether we learned that lesson.

outline.heading: Acute interest, then back to baseline
outline.gist: The pattern is predictable: interest during the acute phase and a week or two after, then a plateau back to the old baseline or lower. The issue now goes beyond the Holy Land and the Palestinian people.

outline.heading: The ignored will of a nation
outline.gist: The weekly protests across the globe are far larger than the Palestinian diaspora: the will of a nation told it is background noise because it lacks proper channels of advocacy. So what will change for us as a community?

outline.heading: Clean up your own backyard first
outline.gist: We cannot dictate how Muslim leaders, scholars or businesses respond, but we can change our own conduct and communities. If you cannot make your ideas work for 35,000 Muslims in one city, do not lecture the world on how to fix itself.

outline.heading: Madinah proved the model worked
outline.gist: Had Madinah failed there would be no Islam. Against the tribal system of an undisputed elder, the Prophet built a mixed society with rights, ethics and leadership, and new financial, political and social models, and people came to see it.

outline.heading: Selflessness that visitors came to witness
outline.gist: People thought human greed too powerful to set aside, yet in Madinah wealth was shared even in need and migrants lived in Ansar homes. Visitors came just to see it; a house in order let a few people spread the deen across the old world within thirty years.

outline.heading: Kisra's treasures and a spot that became a splash
outline.gist: When the Prophet promised the treasures of Kisra, people laughed. He knew the order: start with yourself, then locally, then upward. On a time-lapse of history Islam goes from a spot in Madinah to a splash across three continents.

outline.heading: If we cannot care for our own, the claim is hollow
outline.gist: Before preaching to others, we must care for youth, elders, converts, newcomers and those struggling with mental, financial or social health. Claiming to stand for Palestine while doing nothing locally is not honest.

outline.heading: Show me how it works for you
outline.gist: People will say the Quran and the Prophet sound beautiful, so why is it not working for you? The community has to be the evidence, and many who stopped coming have lost that conviction.

outline.heading: Forty years of wandering, or a decision now
outline.gist: Without a house in order, change could take centuries. The Israelites told Musa to go fight with his Lord and were left to wander forty years for a new generation. This generation does not need forty years; it needs a conscious decision.

outline.heading: What was your life about?
outline.gist: In a hundred years everyone in the room will be gone. What purpose did your life serve? That question has to come back to the surface, at any age.

outline.heading: The Prophet's question; Islam as the main project
outline.gist: This is the question the Prophet put to people, and men in their sixties and seventies changed. Islam cannot be a secondary gain: start with yourself and locally, then spread your wings.

outline.heading: Tired of the same complaints
outline.gist: Since he was six he has heard the same problems raised in khutbahs; they only change form. Endless talk with nothing changing has to be taken seriously.

outline.heading: Interlude
Islam is a cause, not only rituals
outline.gist: Islam has to move from exclusively rituals and acts of worship to a cause you live for and, if needed, die for.

outline.heading: Educated just enough to run the machines
outline.gist: Those in control want people educated enough to write code and keep things moving, aware enough to complain, but not enough to call out corruption, oppression, racism or double standards, and kept busy by consumerism.

outline.heading: Chasing bread: a principled people is hard to control
outline.gist: In the Middle East people are kept running after bread all their lives. A population that lives for justice, integrity and fairness is hard to contain, distract, tempt or control.

outline.heading: Why Muslims are labelled; advocate regardless
outline.gist: Muslims are labelled because they are among the last who put principles above status, jobs, reputation and comfort. If we believe in justice, we keep advocating whether the bombing continues or not.

outline.heading: Introducing the laws of victory
outline.gist: Start by cleaning up our own backyard. His new series is the laws of victory: the first ten surahs tell a story of how the Muslims evolve.

outline.heading: Al-Anfal's laws and strength from within
outline.gist: The short Al-Anfal lays down 20 to 23 laws of what a nation must avoid and hold on to; he will take the most relevant ones. When you are weak you cannot help the mistreated; strength must come from within individuals and communities.

outline.heading: Outro

2:259.ar: أَوۡ كَٱلَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرۡيَةࣲ وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا قَالَ أَنَّىٰ يُحۡيِۦ هَٰذِهِ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَاۖ فَأَمَاتَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِاْئَةَ عَامࣲ ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُۥۖ قَالَ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتَۖ قَالَ لَبِثۡتُ يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمࣲۖ قَالَ بَل لَّبِثۡتَ مِاْئَةَ عَامࣲ فَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِكَ وَشَرَابِكَ لَمۡ يَتَسَنَّهۡۖ وَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰ حِمَارِكَ وَلِنَجۡعَلَكَ ءَايَةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِۖ وَٱنظُرۡ إِلَى ٱلۡعِظَامِ كَيۡفَ نُنشِزُهَا ثُمَّ نَكۡسُوهَا لَحۡمࣰ اۚ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُۥ قَالَ أَعۡلَمُ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
2:259.en: Or (bethink thee of) the like of him who, passing by a township which had fallen into utter ruin, exclaimed: How shall Allah give this township life after its death? And Allah made him die a hundred years, then brought him back to life. He said: How long hast thou tarried? (The man) said: I have tarried a day or part of a day. (He) said: Nay, but thou hast tarried for a hundred years. Just look at thy food and drink which have not rotted! Look at thine ass! And, that We may make thee a token unto mankind, look at the bones, how We adjust them and then cover them with flesh! YZXEVob-ZyY.title: Quranic Stories: The Story of Uzayr
YZXEVob-ZyY.one_line: Uzayr's hundred-year sleep over ruined Jerusalem teaches that cities always revive; the real loss is a people forgetting their covenant and teachings.
YZXEVob-ZyY.summary: Speaking as Gaza is under attack, the sheikh tells the story behind the man who passed by a ruined town in Surat al-Baqarah, identified as Uzayr. He gives the context: two centuries after Sulayman, Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Jerusalem and carried its people to Babylon. Uzayr, a pious scholar who had memorised the Torah and possibly a prophet following the law of Musa, is sent to rebuild it, but looking over the ruins he doubts it can ever live again. Allah causes him to sleep for a hundred years, the span in which, the sheikh argues, a generation and its ideas are replaced, which is why a reviver is sent each century. He wakes to his food unspoiled, his donkey raised from bones and Jerusalem rebuilt, but the returned people have lost the Torah, so he leads them to a buried copy and recites it from memory. The lesson he draws is that restoring land, power and buildings happens through the natural course of time, while preserving the covenant is hard and easily lost. A people's true loss is not when their city falls but when they forget who they are, so Muslims watching events today should worry most about whether their descendants will still hold the Quran.

outline.heading: Context: Nebuchadnezzar destroys Jerusalem
outline.gist: Two centuries after Sulayman's kingdom declined, the Babylonian king killed or enslaved Jerusalem's people and carried them to Babylon.

outline.heading: Uzayr's origins and a ruined Jerusalem
outline.gist: Born in southern Iraq, he lived while Jerusalem lay in ruins with few people left.

outline.heading: Jerusalem as the world's barometer
outline.gist: When the Holy Land is ruled justly the world does well; today's racism, apartheid and genocidal intent there mirror a troubled world, with the once oppressed now oppressing.

outline.heading: Who Uzayr was
outline.gist: A pious scholar who had memorised the Torah, possibly a prophet bringing no new law; Allah commanded him to rebuild Jerusalem, a story of hope when hope seems lost.

outline.heading: How could Allah revive this?
outline.gist: After building a single hut he looks over the total ruin from a cave and feels revival is impossible, as a feeling rather than an objection.

outline.heading: Asleep for a hundred years
outline.gist: He sleeps a century, during which the people return and rebuild the city in its beauty.

outline.heading: Why a hundred years matters
outline.gist: A century is enough for one generation's ideas to give way to another's, which is why a reviver is sent every hundred years; none of us will be here in a hundred years.

outline.heading: His food unspoiled, his donkey raised
outline.gist: He sees his food unchanged and watches Allah bring his donkey's bones back to life.

outline.heading: Mocked by the people
outline.gist: Townspeople laugh at a man claiming to have slept a century, so he leads them to where a Torah was buried.

outline.heading: Reviving is easy; keeping the covenant is hard
outline.gist: Life returns through the ordinary cycle without any miracle, but teachings and law can be lost completely, as the Torah had been.

outline.heading: He recites the Torah from memory
outline.gist: They dig out the scroll and follow along as he recites it, and he revives the law of Musa.

outline.heading: Return home and the blind old servant
outline.gist: His family are long dead; a blind woman of 125 asks him to pray for her sight, recognises him and he brings the exiles back from Babylon.

outline.heading: The lesson for us today
outline.gist: Power and control always shift with time; the question is whether people in a hundred years will still know and follow the Quran.

outline.heading: Loss is when you fall, not the city
outline.gist: Losing one's teachings and identity is the real defeat; the Prophet lost nothing when expelled from Makkah and gained Madinah.

outline.heading: Outro
